doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: High school with no jazz teachers; Mike Garson and Steve Lipman
summary: No band director or teacher taught jazz; he learned with friends like Mike Garson and Steve Lipman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: When you were in high school, did you have a band director who was especially hip to these things?

No, not that – we never talked jazz. It was a decent band director, Mr. [?] and Mr. [?Polikov]. I remember them. We were in the dance band. We kind of ran ourselves. But no, I didn’t have any older guy who said, “Listen to this.” I didn’t. I had my friends, Mike Garson, my first friend, piano player. We hunted it together, maybe. And my friend Steve Lipman. He would come and see Trane with me. You had friends, and they’d say, did you hear this record?, did you hear that record? But I would say, more or less, I was on my own. And the teaching, again, remember, there’s no teaching either, because I’m studying with Mr. Shapiro, and that’s certainly not jazz. Not that it was taboo, but it wasn’t – nobody taught jazz then. There was no – eventually I got to [Lennie] Tristano, because he was the only game in town. But nobody taught jazz, really.
